posts.angle: Translate a golfer's visible workaround into a safer gift decision
posts.headline: The thoughtful golf-gift test: what have you actually noticed?
posts.copy: Before buying golf gear, name the workaround: dirty grooves cleaned with a tee, a worn towel, wet grip, or a practice plan that never gets set up. Our guide maps five witnessed frictions to gifts—and tells you when a gift card is smarter.
posts.assetBrief: Original vertical checklist with four illustrated course-day frictions, one check-before-buying line, and no product photography or logos.
posts.altText: Checklist showing four observed golfer frictions: dirty grooves, a worn towel, wet grip, and postponed putting practice.

posts.angle: Show why a coherent pair completes one job instead of adding cart value
posts.headline: A golf gift pair that actually belongs together
posts.copy: Brush first, wipe second. A compact groove brush and a replacement towel perform different parts of one course-day routine. Save the pair only if both current tools are missing or worn; otherwise choose the anchor alone.
posts.assetBrief: Original two-step brush-then-wipe diagram with distinct item roles, an 84 coherence score, and a clear choose-only-one fallback.
posts.altText: Two-step diagram showing a golf brush loosening groove debris and a towel wiping moisture from the club.

posts.angle: Make the recipient observation and rejection condition equally prominent
posts.headline: Buy this golf brush only if you have seen this exact workaround
posts.copy: Great fit: they scrape groove dirt with a tee or complain about an awkward brush. Skip it: they already carry a water brush they like or do not use a bag. Current owner reviews also make durability a check, not an assumption. Thoughtfulness is the fit signal, not the category label.
posts.assetBrief: Original split card with green Buy if and coral Skip if columns, a simple tee and brush line illustration, and no merchant imagery.
posts.altText: Buy-if and skip-if card for a compact golf brush based on whether the recipient improvises groove cleaning.

posts.angle: Separate a true all-weather golfer from a generic golf recipient
posts.headline: Does your golf friend actually play through bad weather?
posts.copy: Rain gloves require both the FootJoy fit profile—Regular Pair or Cadet Pair—and size from S through XL. A full-size umbrella requires weather habits and storage. This decision flow keeps a useful all-weather gift from becoming the wrong fit for a fair-weather or minimalist golfer.
posts.assetBrief: Original vertical yes-no decision flow covering wet conditions, FootJoy fit profile, size, umbrella storage, and a gift-card fallback.
posts.altText: Decision flow asking about wet-weather play, Regular or Cadet FootJoy fit, glove size, and storage for a full-size golf umbrella.

posts.angle: Turn hobby specificity into a confident list of gifts not to guess
posts.headline: The golf gifts not to surprise a selective golfer with
posts.copy: Clubs, balls, shoes, bags, grips, rangefinders, and swing technology can all be great—when the exact preference is known. Without it, solve a witnessed small annoyance or fund the choice they want to make themselves.
posts.assetBrief: Original no-guessing checklist with seven equipment categories, one observed-friction alternative, and one gift-credit fallback.
posts.altText: Checklist of preference-heavy golf equipment categories that should not be guessed as surprise gifts.

posts.angle: Teach the observed-friction framework through five golfer moments
posts.headline: Five golf gifts that say 'I noticed'
posts.copy: The friend who cleans grooves with a tee. The towel that should have retired. The all-weather round. The putting plan with no setup. Five researched gifts, five reasons to skip, and one pair that completes a real job.
posts.assetBrief: Seven original slides: thesis, five friction scenes, and final pre-gift checklist; use illustrations and typography only.
posts.altText: Carousel summarizing five observed golfer frictions and the check-before-buying rule for each gift.

posts.angle: Open with the wrong generic-golf-gift pattern and resolve it with observation
posts.headline: Stop buying your golf friend random golf stuff
posts.copy: Hook: your golf friend does not need another novelty gadget. Show four quick workarounds—a tee cleaning grooves, a worn towel, a wet grip, and an unused practice plan—then ask one question: which problem have you actually seen?
posts.assetBrief: Original short-form storyboard using staged generic props only; no third-party product images, logos, course footage, or hands-on performance claims.
posts.altText: Short video storyboard contrasting random golf gadgets with four observable course-day friction points.
